fixes.subject: b1c1-audit-s03
fixes.description: They play dead while mounted troops pass directly through the battlefield.

fixes.subject: b1c1-audit-s06
fixes.description: They physically encounter Akemi among battlefield corpses before reaching her home.

fixes.subject: b1c1-audit-s08
fixes.description: Matahachi is treated for illness and Takezo tends his bullet wounds during an extended stay.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s04
fixes.description: Oko gives Takezo a heavy black-oak practice sword taken from battlefield plunder.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s05
fixes.description: Oko enters Takezo's sleeping space at night and makes a sexual advance that he rejects.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s08
fixes.description: Matahachi kills one unnamed member of Temma's group during the fighting.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s09
fixes.description: The household warns that Temma's younger brother Kohei is more dangerous and may retaliate.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s10
fixes.description: Matahachi and Oko become increasingly intimate during the final night at the house.

fixes.subject: b1c2-audit-s12
fixes.description: Takezo wakes to the empty house, finds Oko's red comb and thinks of Otsu.

fixes.subject: b1c3-audit-s05
fixes.description: Otsu reacts emotionally to memorial inscriptions treating Takezo and Matahachi as dead.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-s01
fixes.description: Heita tells Osugi that Otsu saw Takezo at the festival.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-s02
fixes.description: Osugi and Otsu go to Ogin's house seeking Takezo and information about Matahachi.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-s04
fixes.description: Otsu reaches Takuan at Shippoji and reports Ogin's arrest.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-s06
fixes.description: Takezo questions a charcoal maker and learns Ogin was arrested and is rumored to be at Hinagura.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-s07
fixes.description: Takezo returns physically to Shippoji, sees the Himeji officer assaulting Otsu, strikes him and escapes as the alarm is raised.

fixes.subject: b1c5-audit-s02
fixes.description: The letters trigger a severe emotional crisis before Takuan intervenes.

fixes.subject: b1c5-audit-s03
fixes.description: Takuan confronts the Himeji officer over the failed manhunt and establishes his personal connection to Ikeda Terumasa.

fixes.subject: b1c5-audit-s04
fixes.description: The officer agrees that Takuan may decide Takezo's fate if he captures him within three days; Takuan stakes his own life on failure.

fixes.subject: b1c5-audit-s06
fixes.description: They remain in the mountain area for three days waiting for Takezo; Otsu's flute becomes part of the encounter that draws him near.

fixes.subject: b1c6-audit-s02
fixes.description: Villagers debate Takezo's fate; Osugi demands harsh punishment and the Himeji officer tries to reclaim official authority.

fixes.subject: b1c6-audit-s03
fixes.description: Takuan invokes the prior bargain and prevents the officer from taking custody.

fixes.subject: b1c6-audit-s05
fixes.description: Osugi pressures Otsu to enter the Hon'iden household as Matahachi's bride before his return.

fixes.subject: b1c6-audit-s06
fixes.description: Takuan challenges Takezo's ideas of strength, courage and the samurai way while he is bound in the tree.

fixes.subject: b1c6-audit-s08
fixes.description: During the storm Otsu repeatedly begs Takuan to release Takezo; he refuses.

fixes.subject: b1c7-audit-s01
fixes.description: Takuan continues the confrontation over courage and human purpose until Takezo explicitly asks to live and change.

fixes.subject: b1c7-audit-s05
fixes.description: Heita reports the escape; Osugi mobilizes relatives and tenants and begins pursuit with Gonroku.

fixes.subject: b1c7-audit-s06
fixes.description: A border official refuses the large pursuit party; only Osugi and Gonroku continue across.

fixes.subject: b1c8-audit-s04
fixes.description: The text retrospectively identifies the officer who made the capture bargain as Aoki Tanzaemon; earlier 'Himeji captain/Scraggly Beard' scenes belong to this same person.

fixes.subject: b1c8-audit-s11
fixes.description: Otsu explains that Takuan rescued her from the ravine near Mikazuki and arranged her work near Hanada Bridge.

fixes.subject: b2c1-audit-s07
fixes.description: Matahachi remembers Otsu, his mother and Miyamoto, recognizes his decline and resolves to leave Oko.

fixes.subject: b2c1-audit-s08
fixes.description: Matahachi leaves by the kitchen door, returns for money, searches Oko's belongings and remains trapped by indecision.

fixes.subject: b2c4-audit-s02
fixes.description: Jotaro states that his father is Aoki Tanzaemon, a former 2,500-koku samurai who lost his status; Musashi explicitly reflects on his own role in Tanzaemon's misfortune.

fixes.subject: b2c4-audit-s03
fixes.description: Jotaro asks to become Musashi's follower and Musashi conditionally agrees if the boy obtains his master's consent.

fixes.subject: b2c5-audit-s02
fixes.description: From the written name and Jotaro's description, Akemi realizes Miyamoto Musashi is Takezo and revives her long-held hope of seeing him again.

fixes.subject: b2c5-audit-s08
fixes.description: Otsu accepts largely because the Yagyu household may have records or visitors who can lead her to Musashi.

fixes.subject: b2c6-audit-s07
fixes.description: Although Musashi won physically against Agon, he leaves feeling spiritually outclassed by Nikkan.

fixes.subject: b2c6-audit-s12
fixes.description: The widow gives Musashi clothing and permits Jotaro to keep an old Noh mask before they prepare to leave.

fixes.subject: b2c6-audit-s13
fixes.description: The dumpling-maker's wife warns that Hozoin priests and ronin are waiting toward Hannya Plain because forged insults have been attributed to Musashi; he chooses to leave anyway.

fixes.subject: b2c8-audit-s02
fixes.description: Musashi explains that serious martial study includes geography, agriculture, customs, governance and the condition of a lord's territory, not just fighting.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s05
fixes.description: Otsu gives the rejected peony to Kocha rather than taking it back to the castle.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s09
fixes.description: Sekishusai learns Denshichiro failed even to notice the peony's cut and judges that the Yoshioka house effectively ended with Kempo.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s10
fixes.description: At the Yagyu dojo Kizaemon drives students through severe Shinkage-style training, illustrating the household's standard.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s11
fixes.description: Jotaro enters the castle and forces Kizaemon to read Musashi's unusual letter asking who made the peony cut.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s12
fixes.description: The Yagyu retainers compare the two cuts, learn Sekishusai made the original and infer that Musashi has unusual perception.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s13
fixes.description: The retainers decide to invite Musashi informally to the Shin'indo for food, sake and martial conversation.

fixes.subject: b2c9-audit-s14
fixes.description: While waiting, Jotaro provokes and strikes the large black dog Taro; the dog attacks and injures him.

fixes.subject: b2c10-audit-s07
fixes.description: Jotaro finds Taro and kills the dog as revenge for the earlier attack.

fixes.subject: b2c11-audit-s06
fixes.description: Otsu and Jotaro chase Musashi onto the Tsukigase-Iga back road until he disappears into wooded foothills.

fixes.subject: b2c11-audit-s09
fixes.description: Otsu tells Takuan she remains determined to find Musashi; Takuan warns that her fixation may lead her toward self-destruction.

fixes.subject: b2c11-audit-s10
fixes.description: Otsu refuses to remain peacefully at Koyagyu; Jotaro chooses to continue with her after retrieving his mask, while Takuan accepts that he cannot stop them.

fixes.subject: b3c1-audit-s07
fixes.description: A mendicant priest laments his lost samurai status, his conduct involving Otsū and the harm done to his only son Jōtarō.

fixes.subject: b3c5-audit-s06
fixes.description: In delirium Akemi mentions Musashi, New Year's and Gojō Bridge, revealing the expected meeting.

fixes.subject: b3c9-audit-s08
fixes.description: The narration explicitly identifies Shishido Baiken as Tsujikaze Kōhei and confirms Tsujikaze Temma was his brother.

fixes.subject: b3c10-audit-s08
fixes.description: Sannojō guides them above Kaga Village to Makado Pass and directs them toward Seto in Otsu.

fixes.subject: b3c12-audit-s01
fixes.description: Creditors crowd the Yoshioka school while Seijūrō hides and Ryōhei drives them out by intimidation.

fixes.subject: b4c1-audit-s09
fixes.description: Kojirō continues to control and taunt Akemi while she fears his cruelty but remains in his company.

fixes.subject: b4c4-audit-s03
fixes.description: Matahachi gives Denshichirō a distorted story portraying Musashi as the abductor of his fiancée and himself as a revenge-seeker.

fixes.subject: b4c17-audit-s03
fixes.description: At Hachidai Shrine Musashi nearly prays for supernatural protection, stops himself and reframes the episode as a warning against hidden attachment to life.

fixes.subject: b5c18-audit-s04
fixes.description: Musashi uses the incident to teach Iori that etiquette restrains people's bad side and is essential in crowded civic life.

fixes.subject: b5c18-audit-s07
fixes.description: When horse trader Kumagorō threatens him over noise complaints, Musashi silently plucks live flies from his soba with chopsticks, causing the traders to retreat.

fixes.subject: b5c19-audit-s02
fixes.description: Kōsuke explains Kōetsu's teaching that the craftsman's real work is polishing the samurai's soul and that a sword exists to preserve integrity and order, not delight in killing.

fixes.subject: b5c19-audit-s03
fixes.description: Musashi accepts the criticism and recognizes that he has not adequately considered the moral spirit of the sword he carries.

fixes.subject: b5c22-audit-s05
fixes.description: Jūrō and the Hangawara men initially mock Osugi's sutra but become emotionally overwhelmed by its description of parental sacrifice and filial neglect.

fixes.subject: b5c24-audit-s07
fixes.description: Iori blames his long delay on a fox; Musashi reframes the punishment as Iori's own invisible conscience reacting to his choices.

fixes.subject: b5c25-audit-s05
fixes.description: Kagenori tells Yogorō that his military science is now aimed at peace and stability and that he needs the right mature man to receive it because Yogorō is not ready.

fixes.subject: b6c4-audit-s06
fixes.description: Umpei, an experienced well-digger boss working for the shōgun's castle project, again offers Matahachi higher-paid work inside the castle grounds.

fixes.subject: b6c5-audit-s05
fixes.description: Shinzō reports that Kagenori has died and that Yogorō also died after going alone to seek revenge on Kojirō.

fixes.subject: b6c5-audit-s06
fixes.description: With Yogorō dead, Shinzō says adoption proceedings arranged through his father and Munenori will make him Kagenori's heir and successor to the Obata name.

fixes.subject: b6c6-audit-s09
fixes.description: Musashi internally rejects the sword of conquest and mere technical instruction, defining the Way instead as a means to establish order, protect and refine the spirit and ultimately contribute to peace and good government.

fixes.subject: b6c9-audit-s08
fixes.description: Pressed by Iori's questions about loyal and rebel dead, Musashi concludes that a genuine samurai and swordsman must possess compassion and an appreciation of life's poignancy, not merely destructive skill.

fixes.subject: b6c12-audit-s08
fixes.description: Iori follows Jōtarō, denounces him as a thief and eventually fights him near the Musashino cabin, using Musashi's eye-training lesson.

fixes.subject: b6c12-audit-s09
fixes.description: The boys discover that both regard Musashi as their teacher; their hostility gives way to shocked recognition even though mistrust remains.

fixes.subject: b6c12-audit-s10
fixes.description: Still struggling in a tree, Iori and Jōtarō fall together and are knocked unconscious.

fixes.subject: b6c12-audit-s14
fixes.description: Jōtarō admits helping Daizō rob the treasure house while claiming the theft serves the public; Takuan attacks the logic of a half-educated do-gooder imposing his own idea of social good.

fixes.subject: b6c13-audit-s02
fixes.description: Osugi appears at the mansion and gives Shinzō a long denunciation of Musashi, citing Sekigahara, alleged crimes and the Otsū dispute to argue he is unfit to teach the shōgun.

fixes.subject: b6c17-audit-s02
fixes.description: Musashi says the Way of the Sword and good government should ultimately align, but he now sees that governance requires a perfect blending of military and literary arts and that he still has much to learn from the country itself.

fixes.subject: b7c12-audit-s02
fixes.description: Praise of Musashi provokes Kojirō into repeated public attacks on Musashi's character and Ichijōji conduct, helping turn rivalry into expected confrontation.

fixes.subject: b7c12-audit-s09
fixes.description: Despite outward confidence, Kojirō increasingly thinks about Omitsu, his dead mother and the possibility of his own death.

fixes.subject: b7c13-audit-s03
fixes.description: Gempachi recognizes Matahachi from the period when he falsely called himself Sasaki Kojirō; Matahachi now looks back on that impersonation with shame rather than pride.

fixes.subject: b7c13-audit-s07
fixes.description: Surrounded by admirers and gifts, Kojirō becomes psychologically burdened by the repeated inner command that he must win.

fixes.subject: b4c7-audit-arrival
fixes.description: Musashi reaches Rengeōin, warms himself in the temple and takes the veranda position before revealing himself.

fixes.subject: b2c6-audit-jotaro-arrival
fixes.description: Jōtarō reaches the boardinghouse where Musashi is already lodging; only the boy makes this arrival.

fixes.subject: b7c11-audit-aoki
fixes.description: The directly narrated flashback stages Aoki in Himeji helping plan the attempt to contact Musashi’s ship.

fixes.subject: b1c4-audit-summons
fixes.description: Osugi sends her daughter-in-law to summon armed help while Takezō is bathing.

fixes.subject: b2c1-audit-messenger
fixes.description: A Yoshioka messenger reports that Musashi is at the school defeating its men and waiting for Seijūrō.
